meta.market: Manhattan, Midtown East and Lower Manhattan Class B office conversions
meta.note: Default market assumptions for the HBU engine. Every figure here is a starting point the user can override on screen. Calibrated against the 305 East 46th Street analysis (Apr 2026): rental conversion NOI about $5.4M, stabilized value about $108M at a 5.0% cap, conversion cost about $57M, yield on conversion cost 9.3%. Update the numbers, not the engine.

office.label: Office repositioning
office.marketRentBasis: Class B Midtown East asking rents, 2026
office.opexBasis: Operating expenses excluding real estate taxes, $/RSF/yr
office.taxesBasis: Full real estate taxes, $/RSF/yr; overridden by the building input when given
office.repositioningCapexBasis: Lobby, elevators, systems, amenity floor; $/gross SF
office.leasingCostBasis: Tenant improvements plus commissions on newly leased space, $/RSF
office.profitTargetBasis: Developer margin on total cost used in the land residual

condo.label: Condo conversion
condo.efficiencyBasis: Sellable SF as a share of gross SF after cores, corridors, amenities
condo.selloutBasis: Blended sellout for a Midtown East conversion, $/sellable SF, 2026
condo.hardCostBasis: Conversion hard cost, $/gross SF, condo finish level
condo.softCostBasis: Design, permits, legal, insurance, developer overhead as a share of hard cost
condo.salesCostBasis: Brokerage, marketing, transfer taxes and closing as a share of sellout
condo.carryBasis: Construction interest and carry as a share of hard plus soft cost
condo.profitTargetBasis: Developer margin on gross sellout used in the land residual

rental.label: Multifamily rental conversion (467-m)
rental.efficiencyBasis: Rentable SF as a share of gross SF
rental.marketRentBasis: Market-rate rent for a Class B conversion product in Midtown East, $/RSF/yr, 2026
rental.affordableRentBasis: Weighted average 80% AMI rent per unit per month under 467-m, 2026 income limits
rental.opexBasis: Operating expenses excluding real estate taxes, $/RSF/yr
rental.taxesBasis: Full real estate taxes before exemption, $/RSF/yr; overridden by the building input when given
rental.hardCostBasis: Conversion hard cost, $/gross SF, rental finish level; with soft, contingency and carry this lands near $400/gross SF all-in
rental.capRateBasis: Stabilized Manhattan multifamily with a long tax exemption, 2026
rental.targetYieldBasis: Untrended yield on total cost a rental developer needs; drives the land residual

467m.name: 467-m office-to-residential tax exemption
467m.eligibility: Commercial building built before 1991 in a district that permits residential; at least 25% of units affordable at a weighted average of 80% AMI with none above 100% AMI; construction start before mid-2031

cityOfYes.name: City of Yes conversion eligibility
cityOfYes.eligibility: Buildings built before 1991 may convert to residential citywide in districts where residential is permitted, under the conversion rules of Article I, Chapter 5

recommendation.rule: Highest land residual value wins by default: that is the price a developer could pay for the building under each use. Ties within 5% go to the higher return on cost, then the shorter path to stabilization. The user can rank by value created (stabilized value or sellout over total cost) instead.
